title: Four homogenised SST products have larger mean trend gaps against held-out references in 2005-2024
abstract: We tested four SST products from a published seven-product blind homogenisation. We kept the mean product-minus-reference trend separate from the spread between products. In 2005-2024 at 60S-60N, correction reduces slope spread by 87-90%, but increases the mean trend gap. The corrected mean is 0.014 C per decade below HadSST4.2 and 0.026 below Roemmich-Gilson Argo on their separate sampling designs. Conditional block-bootstrap intervals exclude zero. The tropical Argo gap is 0.072 C per decade. The gaps persist from 2008 and without 2023-2024. A fixed July 2016 level term accounts for the Argo gap without a significant remaining linear drift. Against HadSST4.2 in 1985-2024, the mean gap is consistent with zero. An exact identity and numerical injection show that the spread of paired trend differences contains no information about the reference trend. Thus convergence alone cannot validate the shared trend. The analysis does not assign the gaps to product error or reference error, does not refit the correction, and does not reject warming acceleration. Intervals omit correction and reference systematic uncertainty.

display.caption: Mean product-minus-reference trends in 2005-2024. Bars give conditional 95% intervals with 24-month blocks. Raw and corrected products use the same four-product mean.
Twelve-month centred means of corrected product-minus-reference residuals. Each curve is centred over 2005-2024; the two references have separate sampling designs.

citations.reason: We use two released aggregate tables. Long-period HadSST agreement is supported; slope-spread reduction is insufficient to validate the common recent trend.
